title: Developer-Bridge Prefetch & Typed Stream Orchestration (PRD - sketch)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working PRD sketch that explores a low-friction developer-facing surface for: incremental streaming with typed frames, prefetch-friendly SDK patterns (developer-bridge), and deterministic tool-call handshakes that keep latency SLOs tight while enabling structured output validation.

Context & motivation:
- Teams building embed/assistant features are asking for: predictable partial results, a way to pre-declare tool intents (so we can prefetch upstream data), and SDK ergonomics that make fallbacks easy for clients.
- Current hosted streaming surfaces are flexible but put the responsibility for prefetching & orchestration on the client. That leads to duplicated logic and missed optimizations on server (we could pre-warm caches, reserve KV, and select lower-cost model variants earlier).
- Goal: enable a thin "developer-bridge" layer in the SDK + lightweight server contract that advertises tool intents and typed output expectations up-front so the platform can prefetch/collocate and the client can receive resumes/checkpoints with strong validation.

Success metrics (observable):
- Developer time to integrate: target < 2 hours for a basic tool+stream usage example (measured via onboarding lab).
- Latency: end-to-end median response time for first actionable frame improved by 25% for workloads where prefetch applied.
- Cost: per-token unit cost reduction 8–12% on modal workloads due to prefix caching & prefetch.
- Reliability: tool-call error rate during streaming reduced by 30% via pre-validated handshakes and typed fallbacks.

Non-goals:
- Full orchestration engine or saga semantics for complex multi-step tool graphs (out of scope; we support local deterministic fallback policy only).
- Replacing existing streaming API; this is an opt-in additional surface and SDK helper.

High-level design overview:
1) Intent-to-prefetch header (opt-in): clients can include a lightweight JSON-LD-like manifest in the initial request describing up to N tool intents (e.g., "lookup-user-profile", "call-db-index:orders"). The server uses this to warm caches, pre-resolve credentials (if allowed), and route to a preferred model shard.
2) Typed frames and partial schemas: responses are emitted as ordered frames with a frame_type tag (text_delta, structured_action, assertion, checkpoint). Each structured_action includes a declared schema_version and a short hash for verification.
3) Fanout-safe tool handshake: when the model decides to call a tool, the server emits a tool_call frame with a deterministic call_id and an intent fingerprint. The SDK can either accept auto-administered prefetch results (if previously authorized) or pause and surface a synchronous hook for client mediation.
4) Snapshot/resume semantics: every checkpoint frame contains a reproducible snapshot id + minimal context necessary for resume (last N tokens, KV pointers). This enables clients to reconnect and resume from the same logical point with consistent tool ordering.

API contract sketches (examples):
- Request headers/body (JSON):
  {
    "prompt": "Summarize account activity and fetch last invoice",
    "bridge_intents": [
      {"id": "user_lookup", "type": "lookup", "scope": "user:123", "prefetch": true},
      {"id": "billing_fetch", "type": "http_get", "url_pattern": "https://api.mgmt/company/{company_id}/invoices", "prefetch": false}
    ],
    "response_schema": {"type":"oneOf","variants":["text","structured_action"]}
  }

- Stream frames (server -> client):
  - frame_type: text_delta, payload: "..."
  - frame_type: tool_call_proposal, call_id: "c-1", intent: "user_lookup", requires_user_mediation: false
  - frame_type: tool_result, call_id: "c-1", status: "ok", result_schema_hash: "sha256:abc...", preview: {"name":"Ava Chen","tier":"pro"}
  - frame_type: structured_action, action_type: "compose_reply", payload_schema_version: "v2", content: { ... }
  - frame_type: checkpoint, snapshot_id: "s-20241003-01", resume_cursor: "token-345"

SDK ergonomics (developer-bridge helpers):
- Opt-in facade: SDK exposes a DeveloperBridge class that accepts the initial manifest (bridge_intents) and manages prefetch life-cycle.
- Hook model: on_tool_proposal(call_id, meta) -> return {"allow_auto": true} or {"pause_for_mediation": true, "ui_hint": "confirm-data"}. The default client behavior is permissive if the manifest marked prefetch:true and the account has previously granted prefetch scope.
- Lightweight validators: SDK ships a typed-schema validator that ensures structured_action frames match declared schema_version. Validation runs in the client and optionally can be configured to fail-fast or fallthrough.
- Resume Manager: SDK keeps durable checkpoints in local storage (encrypted) and can reattach with resume_cursor when connectivity returns.

Observability and telemetry design:
- Mandatory telemetry frames: tool_call_proposal, tool_result, schema_mismatch, resume_event, prefetch_hit/miss. These are emitted to the Console with token-level attribution, but we avoid shipping payloads by default (only metadata + small previews).
- Sampled debug mode: developers can opt into full payload logging for a session (useful for integration lab).
- Cost attribution: prefetch hits are credited to the request and surfaced as a separate cost line item (prefetch-api + token savings).

Operational considerations & security:
- Prefetch scope enforcement: bridge_intents that would fetch customer data must be gated by customer consent and allowed domains. We add KMS-backed token scoping so prefetch creds are short-lived and auditable.
- Rate limits: we separate prefetch quota from runtime quota to avoid accidental overconsumption (prefetch calls count against a configurable prefetch budget).
- Fallbacks: when prefetch fails, the model receives an explicit "prefetch_miss" signal to choose an alternate plan (short summary, ask user to retry, or continue with a lower-fidelity result).

Developer experience examples (quick-start):
- 15-min lab: create a bridge manifest, call StreamingClient.streamWithBridge(manifest), register on_tool_proposal hook, and render structured_action frames. Ship sample code in onboarding repo.
- Post-integration checklist: register allowed prefetch domains in Console, set prefetch budget, add schema artifact referencing a Confluence entry.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (experiments, 2 sprints): internal dev-preview with SDK-only hook and server-side no-op (no prefetch). Collect UX feedback.
- Phase 1 (beta, 6 weeks): enable server prefetch for partner customers, expose prefetch budget in Console, and add telemetry.
- Phase 2 (general availability): full telemetry, SLA docs, and polished SDK surface across languages.

Open questions & tradeoffs (TODOs):
- How large should a bridge manifest be? (N=5 vs N=20) — affects prefetch cost/routing complexity.
- Canonical schema versioning strategy for structured_action: embed full JSON Schema or use registry pointer?
- Client privacy model: preview vs full payload—what's the default and how to make it simple for first-time users?
- Should the SDK proactively fetch credentials for downstream tool proxies or only helm prefetch with server-side creds?

Risks:
- Misuse of prefetch (excessive background requests) increases costs — mitigate via quotas, UI warnings, and sensible SDK defaults (prefetch disabled in free tier).
- Schema drift: model outputs not conforming to declared schemas could break clients — mitigation: sampled validation, client-side fallbacks, and per-schema regression alerts.

Next steps (concrete):
- Product: finalize manifest grammar and prefetch budget UX (owner: Marcus). Deadline: 2024-10-17.
- Eng: spike server prefetch + checkpoint proto (owner: Diego). Run internal lab with 3 demo apps. Deadline: 2024-10-24.
- DX/devrel: build 15-min onboarding lab and a code sandbox (owner: Lina). Deadline: 2024-11-07.

Notes to self / meeting cliff-notes:
- Talk to SRE about resume overheads (we may need lightweight sticky routing).
- Coordinate with security on KMS scoping for prefetch tokens.
- Ask infra: can we tag prefetch requests for intra-cluster data-plane routing?

References & appendices:
- Sketch of frame proto (informal) and resume cursor examples will be attached to Confluence: CONFLUENCE-PRD-DEVBRIDGE.
- Related: see JIRA-API-9821 for telemetry events mapping.

Rough acceptance criteria for beta:
- SDK: DeveloperBridge available in JS + Python with hook API and resume manager.
- Server: prefetch hot-path enabled for 2 test customers, telemetry hooks emitted, prefetch budget enforced.
- Docs: onboarding lab + console controls published.

This is an iterative sketch. Expect multiple follow-ups; marking as draft and will convert to formal PRD after Phase 0 learnings.
